We use the \"Lumped\" average velocity a: When ignoring the actual velocity and tempurature of a delicate fluid like blood or liquid choclate the fluid near the walls is ignored. For example, choclate near the wall of a pan would overheat faster compared to the center which can lead to the chocolate burning. This issue of the chocolate buring is fixed by using a double boiler so that the temperature is more uniform which reduces hot spots that would be found if the chocolate was heat directly in a pan. The double boiler or water bath approach is a way to prevent overheating near the walls and to manage the non uniform temperature and velocity profiles that lumped analysis ignores.
You have two options: Constant Surface T: Constant heat flux is chepater to implement and monitor in a startup scenario with a limited budget. Constant heat flux can be measured from a given supply with a known electrical power, like a heater which can control the temperature of the surfvace. A constant surface temperature would require sensors and feedback controls to monitor the surface temperature while would lead to additional cost and complexity, making constant heat flux a better option when limited to a budget.
The \"Logarithmic Mean Temperature Diffe: A simple arithmetic mean is good enough when the inlet and outlet has a very small temperature difference which creates a linear relationship. When the error between the LMTD and simple arithmetic mean are small it is justifiable tol use simple arithmetic mean to get quick estimates as the added complexity of LMTD is not justified. For example, in HVAC preliminary design, using estimates for equipment or load calcualtions is justified since it is fast and simplifies time and analysis before moving to a more detailed analysis during the design and development stage, where LMTD is more preferred.
